text:
jamie: Heads-up — we need to triage a batch of customer-driven asks into the Q3 initiative board. Main asks: lower-latency kernel option for conversational customers, stricter KV cache eviction policy for finance workloads, and a canary plan for quantized attention kernels.

alex: Can you paste the customer SLAs? we should map them to acceptance criteria.

jamie: @alex copied: Customer A needs p95 < 120ms for short chat (<= 128 tokens), Customer B wants reproducible outputs with deterministic fallback and audit logs.

taylor: Quick thoughts — low-latency kernel will help A but may increase token-cost. We should specify allowed quality regression (e.g., BLEU/semantic fallback) and a rollback path.

matt: For KV eviction: suggest `evict: lru` with priority pinning for `system` prefixes + metric: tail latency increase < 8ms after pinning. Also need an opt-out per-tenant config.

nina: Can we bundle these into a single PRD or separate mini-PRDs? they have different owners.

jamie: My proposal: one initiative card "Serving QoS: latency + correctness controls" with 3 sub-PRDs (kernel, kv-policy, quant-attn). Each sub-PRD: requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout checklist.

priyanka: +1. For acceptance criteria examples:
- Kernel: p95 short-chat <= 120ms on dedicated XPU profile, regression on sample evals <= 2% on semantic sims, automatic fallback to stable kernel in <200ms if error rate spike > 0.5%.
- KV policy: no more than 5% increase in avg token latency at 95th percentile under 95th percentile load, and per-tenant opt-out works end-to-end.
- Quant-attn: end-to-end quality delta measured on 1000 prompt set, failure-safe route back to full-precision within 300ms.

alex: We need explicit test artifacts: perf harness commands, sample promptset S3 path, and a canary rollout spec. e.g.:
```
perf/run.sh --kernel=fast-attn --profile=short-chat --rps=500
```
Promptset: s3://redwood-evals/q3/serve-qos/short-chat-1k.jsonl

matt: Rollout checklist draft:
- Feature flag gated
- Canary 1% internal traffic for 24h -> monitor errors & lat / cost delta
- Canary 10% external customers with opt-in -> 48h
- Auto rollback criteria: error rate > 0.5% or p95 regression > 15% of baseline

nina: Who owns the canary infra and test harness updates? Without that we can't hit dates.

jamie: Owner proposals: kernel -> @taylor, kv-policy -> @matt, quant-attn -> @priyanka. Canary infra -> eng-infra (I'll ping them after this thread).

priyanka: Edge cases to capture in PRD: multi-tenant eviction interference (one tenant pins causing others to starve), partial KV mismatch during rolling upgrades, and model mismatch when fallback triggers (ensure tokenization alignment).

rfc-bot: New RFC draft created: rfc/2432106789-serving-qos-triage.md — authors: taylor, matt, priyanka. Link: https://phabricator.redwood/r/r2432106789

alex: Next steps:
1) owners author sub-PRDs with the acceptance criteria above by EOD Friday
2) eng-infra scope for canary by next Wed
3) schedule a 30m triage on Thu to finalize rollout gates

jamie: Cool. I'll add the initiative card and link sub-PRDs. If anyone has objections to the rollback thresholds speak now. Otherwise I'll move to backlog -> planned. :thumbsup:

matt: Fine with thresholds, but let's add a soft cap for cost delta (tokens/sec $) so we can opt to throttle.

priyanka: Agreed. include cost-alert: 20% unit-cost increase triggers manual review.

taylor: All good. I'll open kernel PRD and attach the perf commands + sample eval set.

jamie: Thanks all — updating board now.
